resources.string: Off — this device will not receive emergency alerts
Turning this off blocks all wireless emergency alerts on this device, including earthquake and evacuation alerts.
Shizuku permission is required to change package states.
Shizuku permission was denied. Allow this app under \"Authorized applications\" on the Shizuku home screen, then check again.
This app uses Shizuku, a free open-source app, to turn system apps off and on without root. Please install Shizuku first.
Install \"Shizuku\" (by Xingchen & Rikka) from the Play Store or GitHub. Use the buttons below so you don\'t end up with a look-alike app.
When the install finishes, return to this screen. It checks again automatically and shows how to start Shizuku.
Shizuku is installed but not running. You can start it with just your phone, no computer needed. The first time takes a few extra steps; after that, only the last step is needed.
Turn back on if it is off after a reboot

On Galaxy phones, Wireless debugging can\'t be used while Auto Blocker is on, so Shizuku can\'t start. Newer Galaxy phones may have it on out of the box.\n\nGo to Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker and turn it off. Skip this step if it is already off.
Turning it back on also stops Shizuku if it is running.

Go to Settings → About phone → Software information and tap \"Build number\" 7 times. After entering your PIN you will see \"Developer mode has been turned on\".\n\nSkip this step if it is already on.
While connected to Wi‑Fi, go to Settings → Developer options → Debugging and turn on \"Wireless debugging\". If asked whether to allow wireless debugging on this network, tap Allow.

① In Shizuku, under \"Start via Wireless debugging\", tap \"Pairing\" and allow notifications.\n② Go to Settings → Developer options, tap the \"Wireless debugging\" label to open it, then tap \"Pair device with pairing code\". A 6-digit code appears.\n③ Pull down the notification shade and enter that code in Shizuku\'s notification. You are done when you see \"Pairing successful\".

Tip: enter the code from the notification shade while the code dialog is still open; closing Settings invalidates it. If it stays on \"Searching for pairing service\", remove Shizuku\'s background restrictions.

In Shizuku, under \"Start via Wireless debugging\", tap \"Start\". When the top of the screen says \"Shizuku is running\", come back to this app.\n\nShizuku stops when the phone reboots. Since you are already paired, next time just make sure Wireless debugging is on and do this step.
You can also turn on USB debugging, connect to a computer, and run the adb command shown under \"Start by connecting to a computer\" → \"View command\" in Shizuku.
This screen checks again automatically when you come back.
Not accessible with the current Shizuku privilege
Turn emergency alerts on the watch off and on from this phone. You don\'t need to install anything on the watch.
Looking for a watch on the same Wi‑Fi…

This phone connects to the watch over Wi‑Fi to turn its emergency alerts off and on. You don\'t need a computer or any app on the watch. The first time takes a few extra steps; after that, only steps 1 and 3 are needed.
Put both on the same Wi‑Fi

Connect the phone and the watch to the same Wi‑Fi.\n\nOn the watch, go to Settings → Connections → Wi‑Fi, turn it on and choose the same network as the phone. If the watch is connected to the phone only over Bluetooth, it can\'t be found.
Turn on Developer options on the watch
On the watch, go to Settings → About watch → Software information and tap \"Software version\" 7 times. You will see \"Developer mode turned on\".\n\nSkip this step if it is already on.
Turn on Wireless debugging on the watch
On the watch, go to Settings → Developer options and turn on \"ADB debugging\" and \"Wireless debugging\". If asked whether to allow it on this network, tap Allow.
The watch may turn Wireless debugging off by itself after a while or when Wi‑Fi changes. Check that it is on every time.
Enter the code shown on the watch
On the watch, tap \"Wireless debugging\" to open it, then tap \"Pair new device\". Enter the 6-digit code shown on the watch here.
Keep the code on the watch screen until pairing is done; it becomes invalid if you close it. If the watch asks \"Allow debugging?\", tap Allow.
Looking for the watch and pairing…
No watch was found. Check that it is on the same Wi‑Fi and Wireless debugging is on.
The pairing screen on the watch was not found. Open \"Pair new device\" on the watch and keep the code on screen while you connect.
Pairing failed. Check the code and try again. A new code appears each time you open \"Pair new device\".
The connection to the watch was lost. Check that Wireless debugging is still on and connect again.
Off — the watch will not receive emergency alerts
Turning this off blocks all emergency alerts on the watch, including earthquake and evacuation alerts.
The setting stays even after the watch reboots. You can turn Wireless debugging off on the watch to save battery; turn it back on the next time you want to change this setting.
